reconcile.connective: Commentators distinguish Christ's testimony being inherently true (8:14) from its being legally inadmissible alone (5:31), one even recasting 5:31 as a rhetorical question.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible presses this as a formal contradiction, juxtaposing Jesus's flat denial and later affirmation of his own testimony's validity.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (2013)

excerpts.excerpt_text: If I bear witness of myself, though it is infallibly true (Joh 8:14), yet, according to the common rule of judgment among men, you will not admit it as legal proof, nor allow it to be given in evidence.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Henry explicitly cross-references Joh 8:14 within the same sentence and draws the truth-vs-legal-admissibility distinction that directly resolves the tension.

excerpts.excerpt_text: That which he denied afore, John 5:31, must be taken by a manner of granting, for in that place he framed himself somewhat to the humor of his hearers, which acknowledged nothing in Christ but his humanity, and therefore he was content they should set light by his own witness, unless it were otherwise confirmed. But in this place he standeth for the maintenance of his Godhead, and praiseth his Father, who is his witness, and agreeth with him.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: The Geneva annotators name John 5:31 outright and supply an accommodation-to-hearers reading that reconciles it with 8:14's affirmation.

excerpts.excerpt_text: Bishop Pearce gives a different turn to this verse, by translating it interrogatively, thus: "If I only bear witness of myself, is not my witness true? i.e. is it, on that account, not true? In Joh 8:14, he says, Though I bear record of myself, yet my record is true. And in Joh 8:18, he says, I am one that bear witness of myself."
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Clarke cites all three verses (5:31, 8:14, 8:18) together and offers Bishop Pearce's interrogative rendering as a distinct grammatical harmonization.

pd_work.author: Adam Clarke
pd_work.note: Clarke treats the tension directly, citing 5:31, 8:14, and 8:18 together and presenting Bishop Pearce's interrogative reading of 5:31 as the harmonizing solution. Haley's Alleged Discrepancies could not be confirmed to cover this specific passage, so this row-surfaced harmonizing commentator is used per the spec's fallback.
